notes:
VOLUME MAP (dougherty2008, line ranges from the PDF page markers): front matter and contents 1-330; Ch.1 Introduction, M. V. Dougherty, about 330-895; Ch.2 'Pico on the Relationship of Rhetoric and Philosophy', Jill Kraye, 895-2100; Ch.3 'Pico, Theology, and the Church', Paul Richard Blum, about 2100-3260; Ch.4 'Pico della Mirandola's Philosophy of Religion', Michael Sudduth, 3260-4200; Ch.5 'The Birth Day of Venus: Pico as Platonic Exegete in the Commento and the Heptaplus', Michael J. B. Allen, 4200-5690 (not extracted); Ch.6 'Three Precursors to Pico della Mirandola's Roman Disputation and the Question of Human Nature in the Oratio', M. V. Dougherty, 5697-7570; Ch.7 'Pico on Magic and Astrology', Sheila J. Rabin, 7576-8920; Ch.8 'Pico's Quest for All Knowledge', Carl N. Still, 8922-10070; Ch.9 'A Life in Works', Francesco Borghesi, 10075-about 10935; index about 10940-11173. There is no essay by Stephen Farmer in this volume; Farmer appears only as editor/translator of the 900 Theses cited by the essayists. In each claim the essay is named in pico_locus.ref as '[Author essay]', and the claimant is that essay's author.

AUDIT ITEMS. (1) The earlier audit (A3) cites DOUG l. 7775-7784 for Kabbalistic source dates: VERIFIED. It is Rabin's essay (chapter 7), lines 7777-7782: Sefer Yetsirah 'written between the third and the sixth centuries'; Bahir 'in fact a twelfth-century compilation'; Zohar 'probably written by Moses de Leon in the thirteenth century'; plus Abulafia, Azriel of Gerona, Recanati at 7783-7786 and Mithridates as translator at 7786-7788. See claims dougherty2008 on Rabin. (2) The 'DOUG notes 20-21' the audit cites for De ente et uno are Sudduth's chapter 4, notes 20 and 21 at lines 3573-3574: note 20 is only 'Pico, On Being and the One, 44' (the Miller translation, Bobbs-Merrill 1965, cited in note 3 at lines 3280-3283) and note 21 is only 'Thomas Aquinas, Summa theologiae I, q. 4, a. 2, corp.' The body text that they support is at 3511-3546 (two senses of 'being'; God as ipsum esse). They are therefore support for Sudduth's summary, not an analysis of the Ficino exchange; the essay names Ficino nowhere in that passage. Sudduth's only mention of Ficino is footnote 31 at lines 3718-3723, on the chain of being.

CRUXES AND SURPRISES. (a) Borghesi at 10829-10860 gives the only account in this volume of the occasion of De ente et uno: Poliziano asked Pico to intervene in a dispute between Platonists (Lorenzo de' Medici and Ficino) and Peripatetics; Borghesi hedges ('Pico seemed to disagree with the very principles of the debate'). This should be read against Allen's 'Second Ficino-Pico Controversy' (cited by Dougherty note 65, l. 6446-6450), which is not in this corpus as a separate work. (b) Dougherty at 6423-6424 dates a letter to Barbaro '6 December 1494, two years before the planned Roman debate': internally inconsistent (the debate was planned for 1487; Pico died in November 1494); do not cite that date. (c) Blum's 13 theses list (2193-2249) includes 3>49 on the rational soul as angel, with the commission's qualification; this is the only angelological item among the 13. (d) Still 9341-9351 reads Pico as entertaining Averroist unicity against Ficino and Aquinas, hedged ('apparently'); compare Farmer note 29 at 9370-9372 which says the attribution to Averroes overstates his position. (e) Kraye 1604-1609 says the commission judged thirteen theses 'heretical or of dubious orthodoxy', slightly different from Blum's 'in various degrees condemned'. (f) The introduction (394-398) says the Commento contained an implicit critique of Ficino; Allen's chapter, not mined here, is where that is worked out. (g) Rabin's claim that Pico's turn against astrology may be due to Savonarola (8781-8795) is explicitly speculative and rests on Bellanti, per the text.

OCR: 'fi' ligatures (U+FB01) and words split across lines with a hyphen occur throughout; several page breaks fall inside sentences and interrupt a quotation with a footnote block, so quotations that span a page break are given as two quote entries (e.g. Blum 3023-3040 and Still 9716-9738). Note text cannot always be told from body text in the OCR; footnote numerals are attached to words (e.g. 'Oratio.5'). Warnings left: claimant_mismatch is expected for every essay; one quote_ambiguous at claim 004 (phrase occurs twice, the locator disambiguates).
